modern: Every soul, the philosopher says, is deprived of truth against its will; so in the same way it is deprived of justice and self-control and kindness and everything of the kind. It is most necessary to bear this constantly in mind, for in this way you will be more gentle towards all.
original: Every soul, the philosopher says, is involuntarily deprived of truth; consequently in the same way it is deprived of justice and temperance and benevolence and everything of the kind. It is most necessary to bear this constantly in mind, for thus thou wilt be more gentle towards all.

notification_original: Every soul, the philosopher says, is involuntarily deprived of truth…

explained.summary:
Marcus recalls a saying of Plato, “the philosopher”: no soul is ever deprived of truth willingly. The same holds for justice, self-control, kindness and every virtue. People who lack them do so out of error, not because they want to be bad.

He says this is essential to keep in mind, because it makes you gentler with everyone.
explained.today: When a teenager is surly or a stranger is short with you, it can help to assume they don’t actually want to be like this. That assumption tends to turn irritation into patience.
